      "value": "Overview
--------

Contentful is the sole CMS across all Zimmermann storefronts (HPC-001). It manages editorial content,
banners, size guides, promotional content, and global assets. Integration is via the Contentful Delivery
API (CDA) for all customer-facing pages, with the Contentful Preview API (CPA) available server-side only.

**Architecture:** Single Contentful space with one environment per delivery tier.
Environment IDs match SFCC tier names exactly — no mapping required at runtime.

Environment Topology
--------------------

Six-tier delivery pipeline. Contentful environment IDs map directly to MRT push targets.

| Tier | Name | Contentful Env ID | MRT Push Command | MRT URL |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 & 2 | DEV | `dev` | `npm run push:dev` | zimmermann-dev.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com |
| 3 | TEST | `test` | `npm run push:test` | zimmermann-test.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com (to be created) |
| 4 | OMS INT | `sit` | `npm run push:sit` | zimmermann-sit.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com |
| 5 | STAGE | `staging` | `npm run push:staging` | zimmermann-stg.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com |
| 6 | UAT | `uat` | `npm run push:uat` | zimmermann-uat.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com |
| 7 | PRODUCTION | `master` (via `production` alias) | `npm run push:prod` | zimmermann-production.sfdc-8tgtt5-ecom1.exp-delivery.com |

Promotion order: **dev → test → sit → staging → uat → master**

Alias Strategy & Release Workflow
---------------------------------

Two aliases are maintained and always kept in sync:

* `production` — what MRT production tier uses (`CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID=production`). Flipping this is the zero-downtime release mechanism.
* `master` — Contentful’s built-in alias, kept in sync with `production`.

### Release workflow

1. Create a release environment in the Contentful web UI: clone from the current `production` target, name it `release-YYYY-MM`.
2. Run migrations: `npm run migrate:contentful -- --target release-YYYY-MM`
3. Test against the release environment directly (bypasses the alias).
4. Promote: `npm run promote:alias -- --target release-YYYY-MM` (flips both aliases atomically).
5. Retain the previous environment for 14 days as a rollback target, then delete.

The `production` alias requires the Contentful Enterprise plan. The `master` alias is always available as the built-in fallback.

API Keys & Tokens
-----------------

| Variable | Scope | Local .env | GitHub Actions | MRT |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `CONTENTFUL_SPACE_ID` | Space (shared) | ✓ | Variable | ✓ per tier |
| `CONTENTFUL_ENVIRONMENT_ID` | Per tier | ✓ | Variable per env | ✓ per tier |
| `CONTENTFUL_DELIVERY_TOKEN` | Per env, read-only | ✓ | Variable per env | ✓ per tier |
| `CONTENTFUL_PREVIEW_TOKEN` | Per env, server-side only | ✓ | Secret per env | ✓ per tier |
| `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` | Per user (personal) | ✓ | Secret (CI service account) | **Never** |
| `CMS_WEBHOOK_SECRET` | Per env | ✓ | Secret per env | ✓ per tier |

### CI service account CMA token

Create a dedicated Contentful user (e.g. `contentful-ci@zimmermann.com`), invite as Space Administrator,
log in as that user and generate a Personal Access Token under Account Settings → CMA Tokens.
Store as the `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN` GitHub Actions secret.

### Per-developer setup

Each developer generates their own CMA token: **Contentful → top-right avatar → Account Settings → CMA Tokens → Create personal access token**.
Add it to local `.env` as `CONTENTFUL_MANAGEMENT_TOKEN`. Delivery and preview tokens are space-level — run `npm run config:contentful` to populate them automatically.

--------------------

Locales are created in the `master` environment during bootstrap; cloned environments inherit them automatically. All translatable fields use `localized: true`; structural fields (asset links, product IDs) use `localized: false`.

-----------------------

| --- | --- | --- |
| **Location** | `scripts/contentful/content-types/*.js` | `overrides/app/components/contentful/experiences/*ContentfulDefinition.ts` |

---------------------------------

* **Contentful roles:** Assign a “Content Editor” role on `sit`, `staging`, `uat`, and `master` that can CRUD entries/assets but cannot edit content types. Only the CI service account can modify content types in those environments.
* **Migration runner** calls `detectDrift` automatically before applying. Use `--force` to bypass.

1. Clone the repository
-----------------------

2. Install dependencies
-----------------------

Most other variables (Adyen, Narvar, Google reCAPTCHA, etc.) are not required to start the local dev server. `.env` is gitignored — never commit it, and never add token values to `.env.sample`.

      "value": "This guide is for any developer joining the Zimmermann SFCC build who will use Claude Code CLI. Read it before your first session — it will save you from the most common mistakes.

> Architecture note: this is a slim overrides project on `@salesforce/retail-react-app` v10 — not a fork of the PWA Kit monorepo. All Zimmermann customisations live in `overrides/` and must be TypeScript (`.ts`/`.tsx`). The base template lives in `node_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/` and must not be edited.

1. What Claude Code is — and isn't
----------------------------------

**What it is:** an AI coding agent that runs in your terminal. You give it a task in plain English, it reads your codebase, and it makes code changes directly to your files. It writes components, fixes bugs, adds tests, refactors logic, and explains code.

**What it is not:** - It doesn't understand your team's current sprint, active branches, or verbal agreements - It doesn't know another developer is mid-refactor on the same hook - It doesn't know a shared utility is used by 14 other components - It has no opinion on whether a change is architecturally appropriate for Zimmermann - It will not warn you before overwriting something important unless you've told it what's important

**Practical consequence:** if your prompt is under-scoped, Claude Code will make changes beyond what you intended — including to shared code other developers depend on. The rules in the repo's `AGENTS.md` exist to prevent this.

2. Installation and authentication
----------------------------------

Prerequisites: Node.js 18/20/22/24 LTS, npm 9+, access to the Zimmermann GitHub org.

Defaultbashnpm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code
claude login # opens a browser — use your work email
claude --version # verify

Run your first session read-only: navigate to the repo root, run `claude`, and type "Describe the structure of this codebase without modifying any files."

Two Git hooks (`pre-commit`, `commit-msg`) install automatically via Husky on `npm install`. Never bypass them with `git commit --no-verify`.

3. Always do this before running Claude Code
--------------------------------------------

**3.0 —** New joiners run `/onboarding` first. `/project-init` is a project-level (not per-developer) check of what's still open — most developers won't need it.

**3.1 — Run `/session-start`** at the start of every session. It reads the project's tracking docs, runs a health check script, states where the build is, and asks you to confirm direction before writing any code. Do not write code until it has completed and you've confirmed the next task.

**3.2 — Confirm your branch:**`git branch --show-current`. If `develop` or `main`, stop and create a feature branch first.

**3.3 — Pull the latest from develop:**`git pull origin develop`, even if you pulled this morning.

**3.4 — Write your prompt before you open Claude Code.** It must include the target (feature/page/component, ideally exact file paths), what you want changed and why, and an explicit scope boundary ("do not modify any file other than X"). If you can't name the target or scope boundary, read more of the codebase first, or ask Claude a read-only "explain this flow" question before scoping the change.

4. How to read AGENTS.md
------------------------

Claude Code auto-loads a small set of files at the start of every session:

| File | Role |
| --- | --- |
| `CLAUDE.md` | Stub — re-exports `AGENTS.md` so Claude picks it up |
| `AGENTS.md` | Branch rules, hard rules, stop-and-ask matrix, project-wide behaviours |
| `.claude/rules/conventions.md` | Day-to-day code-writing conventions (naming, imports, components, hooks, stories) |
| `.claude/rules/frozenFiles.md` | Tier 1 — frozen files |
| `.claude/rules/protectedFiles.md` | Tier 2 — protected files |

Everything else (PRDs, memory files, squad-specific scope) is loaded on demand by skills like `/session-start`, `/audit-tier`, or `/scope-check`.

`AGENTS.md` at the repo root is the rulebook for any AI assistant on this project. The same rules are mirrored to Cursor and GitHub Copilot via a sync script.

* **TypeScript only inside `overrides/`** — `.ts`/`.tsx` only; run `npx tsc --noEmit` before finishing any task that touches it.
* **Hard Rules** — absolute prohibitions; if a task requires breaking one, it needs a human, not Claude Code.
* **Tier 1 files** — frozen. Claude won't touch them without explicit instruction, and even then owner approval must be confirmed first.
* **Tier 2 files** — require a second-developer PR review before merging to develop.
* **Squad ownership** — Squad A owns checkout/cart/payments; Squad B owns PDP/PLP/search/account. Message the other squad's lead before touching their territory, even in your own squad's area if it overlaps.

5. The branching rule — why it's non-negotiable
-----------------------------------------------

On `develop`, a bad Claude Code session could break the integration environment for both squads, introduce regressions blocking the next deployment window, corrupt shared hook state, or trigger a failed Lighthouse CI gate. `develop` only receives human-reviewed, PR-approved changes.

**There are no exceptions, including under deadline pressure.**

`--dangerously-skip-permissions` bypasses all edit/shell-command confirmation prompts — it exists for CI automation only. **Never use it on `release/**`, `develop`, or `main`.** If you want to use it to speed up a session, that's a signal to make your prompt more specific, not to remove the safety check.

**Fixing a bug on a release branch:** don't edit the release branch directly — branch off it:

Defaultbashgit checkout release/v0.1.0
git pull origin release/v0.1.0
git checkout -b fix/release-v0.1.0\_short-description
# fix the bug, then:
gh pr create --base release/v0.1.0 --title "fix(scope): SFCC-999 short description"

6. How to scope a prompt — worked examples
------------------------------------------

The quality of your prompt is the single biggest factor in whether Claude Code helps or causes problems.

**Two flavours of "specific":** when you know exact file paths, name them — this is strictly safer and faster. When you don't, name the feature/entry point and the scope boundary, and let Claude expand to the full file list (it pauses for your confirmation).

**Override-first workflow reminder:** if the file doesn't yet exist under `overrides/`, don't bundle the copy + functional change into one prompt — copy and convert first, confirm the override renders, then make the functional change.

**Example — building a new component:**

DefaultnoneCreate a new file at overrides/app/components/backInStockButton/index.tsx
Build a React component that:
- Accepts productId (string) and variantId (string) as props
- Renders a Chakra UI Button with the label "Notify Me"
- On click, calls a placeholder async function handleNotifyMe() that logs the productId and variantId
- Uses Chakra's Button directly (no Tier 1/Tier 2 file imports)
- Defines BackInStockButtonProps at the top of the file
- Co-locate a paired Storybook story with title: 'Commerce/BackInStockButton' and a Default story
Do not modify any existing files. I will wire this into the PDP myself.

**Example — fixing a layout bug in an existing override:**

DefaultnoneIn this file only: overrides/app/pages/checkout/partials/shipping-address.tsx
The Stack component wrapping the address form fields has too much vertical spacing on mobile.
Change the spacing prop from 6 to 3 when the breakpoint is base (mobile).
Do not modify any theme files. Do not modify any other checkout partials. Do not modify any hooks.

**Example — read-only exploration:**

DefaultnoneWithout modifying any files, explain how the Gift With Purchase (bonus product) flow works in
this codebase. Which hook manages the GWP state? Which component renders the selection modal?
Where is the eligibility rule evaluation happening? What SCAPI endpoint is being called?
Search both overrides/ and node\_modules/@salesforce/retail-react-app/.

7. If Claude Code modifies something it shouldn't
-------------------------------------------------

1. **Stop the session** — `Ctrl+C`.
2. **Check what changed** — `git diff --name-only`.
3. **Assess impact** — squad-scoped files: review carefully and continue. Tier 2: flag in the PR description. Tier 1: see step 4.
4. **Revert Tier 1 changes immediately** — `git checkout HEAD -- path/to/the/file.ts`, or `git checkout .` to revert everything.
5. **Notify the file owner** — even after reverting, they need to know it happened.
6. **Refine your prompt and try again** — the most common cause is an under-scoped prompt; rewrite with explicit file paths and "do not modify any other files."

8. Who to contact
-----------------

See [1.2 Team Overview](https://zimmermannworkboard.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/SFCC/pages/261586947) for the current team directory and contacts. Tier 1 and Tier 2 owners are listed in the repo's `AGENTS.md` Contact Map and `.claude/rules/` files.

-----------------------

| Scenario | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| Starting any Claude Code session | Run `/session-start` → check branch → pull develop → write scoped prompt |
| You're on develop or main | Create a feature branch first, no exceptions |
| You need to change a design token | Ask the UI designer — Claude Code does not touch Tier 1 theme files |
| You need to change `useCurrentBasket` | Ask the Integration lead — Tier 1 |

| You're unsure if a file is shared | `grep -r "import.*filename" overrides/` |
| You want Claude to explain code without changing it | Always say "without modifying any files" in your prompt |
| You're hitting a Tier 1 file legitimately | Get owner approval → name the file explicitly → PR it |
| You need a new package dependency | List what you need to the integration team — do not ask Claude to add it |
| Your commit was rejected by the commit-msg hook | Fix the format: `type(scope): description` |
| You introduced a `.js` file in `overrides/` | Stop. Convert to `.ts`/`.tsx` |

I'd missed it originally because I scoped my earlier research to `.docs/` and live Confluence content, not `.env.sample`'s tooling section where `.mcp.json`'s setup is actually documented.
